[DAY2 18:00:32 - DAY2 18:00:58]
"We don't have that many differences," I say. I pass behind Alice and walk to the refrigerator. Shure: "The gas doesn't seem to be much of a problem." Shure: "It shouldn't be a big deal." I move the curtain beside the fridge. "This is..." I say. I kick the power strip on the floor and look at it. "Yes, it can be used," I say. Lucia: "Is this the power for the fridge?" "Yes, just plug it into the wall," I say. I bend down, unplug the power strip, and pick it up.

[DAY4 15:49:33 - DAY4 15:49:57]
I kick the power strip with my foot, turn to look, pick up an extra power strip, and say, "Uh...". I walk around the living room, pull the socket out, and pick up the power strip with my left hand.

[DAY4 15:56:02 - DAY4 15:56:29]
I pause and turn back to the shelf, set the device on the floor, unplug the extra data cables from the power strip and set them aside, then plug the device's data cable into the power strip. Tasha: "Haha, what's up?"

[DAY2 16:48:00 - DAY2 17:48:00]
I began the day with casual conversation at a café alongside Nicous, Choiszt, Katrina, and others, discussing a Border Collie and joking about borrowing it while reviewing details from Choiszt’s phone. This informal interaction set a relaxed tone before shifting to technical matters. I led a team discussion focused on device battery and power management, emphasizing that although devices might run out of battery, data remained secure. I instructed the team to plug in power banks and highlighted the importance of restarting recordings if interrupted, allowing up to a five-minute timing flexibility to maintain overall timeline accuracy. This established clear priorities for ongoing device management and data security.

Returning to my room, I conducted checks on my computer and equipment while coordinating with the team regarding device statuses. I borrowed Katrina’s power bank to troubleshoot power issues, but it was found to lack sufficient charge, prompting ongoing adjustments and inquiries about its functionality. Nicous assisted by packing and handling devices, yet power problems prevented image display and raised concerns over playlist complexity and incomplete data imports. I confirmed with Katrina that some data segments were still pending import, reassured the team that the allocated two-hour recording time was adequate, and encouraged Shure to name the timeline to ensure alignment. The group remained focused on resolving these technical obstacles to maintain workflow continuity.

Using my phone, I instructed Katrina to synchronize her phone’s time before viewing the puppy and monitored her low battery status while reassuring her about charging options. Moving through the living room, I engaged with friends—discussing room decoration ideas with Lucia, appreciating Alice’s paper flower crafting, and conversing about adding color and decorations using fishing nets. Briefly returning to my room, I greeted Choiszt and others, noted the presence of multiple pairs of glasses, and advised Choiszt to open multiple computer pages to manage tasks efficiently, maintaining active coordination with the group to support workflow.

Noticing that Choiszt lacked a mouse, I retrieved one and shared my preference for touchpads. We discussed Apple computer port compatibility for file transfers, and I provided step-by-step guidance as Choiszt operated the computer, addressing questions on device functions and file management. This established a technical groundwork for task execution. Subsequently, I organized hardware by moving boxes onto the bed, coordinated the setup of three units, confirmed a total of 15 units, divided them evenly, and accepted a laptop and hard drive from Nicous to support configuration. I clarified the number of hard drives required and addressed questions about device connections and locations, ensuring a clear equipment arrangement plan.

While operating the computer, I endorsed the method for managing three hard drives and consulted with Xiao Liu and Nicous to allow for a longer break and clearer task pacing. I monitored Choiszt’s progress, ensuring smooth collaboration within the team. After completing setup, I responded to deletion instructions by confirming that security protocols had removed relevant data. I directed the team to review video footage for accuracy and emphasized checking file sizes to validate task completion, thereby securing data integrity and confirming readiness for subsequent steps.

I initiated discussions on computer screen setup, directing the consolidation from multiple split screens into one subdivided into four sections. Addressing suggestions to delete more files or format devices, I organized the workspace by moving a box and operated Choiszt’s computer to familiarize everyone with the display setup, establishing a clear display management plan. Subsequently, I discussed the composition of the mock defense group with Shure, confirming approximately ten participants, volunteer order based on arrival time, and an expected noon completion time. These clarifications established group dynamics and scheduling for upcoming activities.

Monitoring Choiszt and Nicous as they managed data, I noted task progress at approximately 67%. I handled cable arrangements, checked the time, and prepared for photo documentation with Shure guiding friends’ poses. I sent the photos to the boss for review, managing both documentation and social coordination. To assist with incomplete data exports, I offered my hard drive and delegated USB card formatting to the team. After assigning these data handling tasks, I returned to my room to continue overseeing progress.

I managed materials purchased earlier by instructing Shure to collect and review data. I requested Xie Binzhu to retrieve my water bottle, which Nicous then handed to me. I took short breaks to hydrate while maintaining engagement with the team. I observed playful interactions among friends, including Shure searching the fridge and commenting on missing items. Throughout, I monitored Choiszt and others addressing technical issues, maintaining a balance between social exchanges and task oversight.

Assisting with equipment, I retrieved and offered a power bank to Lucia, explained my capacity to connect multiple computers for power supply, and responded to readiness questions. I guided Nicous to handle the fragile power bank carefully. Amid discussions on cable management, I maintained interaction with the group while overseeing technical equipment setup, ensuring safety and efficiency.

Returning to my room, I conversed with Nicous about his academic major, guided Lucia through phone battery management by advising her to wait until it reached 10% charge before starting recording, and coordinated cable and power bank management as Choiszt cleaned up spilled coffee. I fetched water from the kitchen, operated the water bucket after confirming power requirements with Lucia, then went upstairs to fill a container, ensuring proper use and placement. These actions maintained operational readiness and comfort for all involved.

After preparing the water bottle by filling, capping, and relocating it to my room, I joined friends in the living room and coordinated tidying efforts. I outlined plans involving a hot pot meal and gift giving, ensuring all participants understood the sequence of activities. I observed Choiszt and Nicous nearing completion of computer adjustments, managed data cables, and conducted photo sessions with friends posing for gaming-related shots, forwarding images to the boss for review.

During photo and computer tasks, I facilitated posing guidance and photo review, noting that some computer captures remained incomplete. This concluded the documentation and social coordination phase. Observing discussions about slacking off and startup milestones, I experimented with phone photo transfers. Subsequently, I shifted focus to cleaning by coordinating with the cleaning lady and Lucia on trash disposal, organizing the space while managing phone communications to maintain workflow continuity.

Following a phone call, I searched outside for a courier, clarified location details, and identified myself to the individual. I transitioned from indoor organization to delivery logistics, walking quickly while multitasking on calls and messaging. Upon locating black bags, I sent photo updates and entered through the main gate. I inspected my room through a window, took approving photos, and proceeded inside, noting an action camera positioned on a whiteboard while continuing phone use to coordinate with the team.

Inside, I shared photos with Nicous, Katrina, and Shure, advised unplugging and replugging devices to reset connections, and praised technical achievements. I confirmed that plugging in devices would align readiness. Noting that Shure had finished sesame sauce, I moved to Katrina to summarize collaborative technology discussions and task coordination. Finally, I prompted friends in the living room to power on devices, confirmed electricity status with Shure and Lucia, clarified objects under discussion, and engaged in casual talks about shoes and style while scrolling WeChat, maintaining social rapport amidst technical coordination.

After brief remarks, I ate with friends and managed kitchen cleanup, including washing dishes and discarding trash after consulting with Tasha. I acknowledged the cleaned space, confirming completion of household tasks. Katrina suggested seeing the dog before dinner preparation; I confirmed plans with Shure, Katrina, and Choiszt, concluding with arrangements to visit the dog followed by making dinner, ensuring smooth transition between activities.

Entering my room, I carried a plate through the living room to the kitchen, where I placed it in the sink and tidied the living room table. I unpacked a box and organized its contents, including wires, cardboard boxes, and a power strip. During this, I coordinated with Alice, Katrina, and Lucia about cleaning progress, confirming that the upstairs bathroom trash needed changing. We decided to keep one useful box while discarding others, noted a recently arrived unopened JD package for later attention, and discussed item sorting. I coordinated device setup with Choiszt, checked the time with Katrina, and ensured all cleaning and organizing tasks were aligned among the group to maintain efficiency.

While moving toward the entrance using my phone, I discussed sorting boxes and takeout bags with Lucia. Shure confirmed task completion and commented on the thinness of an item. We agreed to discard takeout bags and some boxes, retaining sturdier ones per Lucia’s suggestion, finalizing the sorting plan. I then checked phone batteries with Katrina and Tasha, instructed Tasha to activate her power bank, and coordinated with Shure and Katrina as they planned a short walk, maintaining attention to power availability and charging needs to ensure readiness.

In the living room and kitchen, I assisted Tasha with her phone and power strip, observed item adjustments, and responded to requests while monitoring others. I engaged with Alice and Lucia on decoration plans involving carpets and photo walls, focusing on ocean-themed elements. After accidentally pressing my computer’s power button, I urgently guided Lucia on safely ejecting hard drives by instructing her to use the USB eject function, ensuring no data loss occurred. This resolved an immediate computer safety issue.

I then worked with Lucia to troubleshoot a failed computer pop-up by closing conflicting software (360 software) and testing different devices for security notifications. I coordinated with Tasha via phone regarding a package pickup, confirmed details including landlord involvement, and arranged for the B&B manager to retrieve and deliver it. Throughout this period, I multitasked between computer operations, phone communication, and group coordination to maintain progress on technical and logistical tasks.

Continuing collaboration with Lucia, I verified and managed security pop-ups on multiple computers, adjusted hardware connections, and provided reassurance during her handling of the devices. I instructed her to photograph the computer screens displaying the security prompts to facilitate documentation and group sharing. This process ensured proper understanding and safe management of security notifications across our equipment.

After completing computer tasks, I organized my room by tidying the bed area, arranging cables, storing a laptop, a box, a pillow, and placing a water bottle in a backpack. I adjusted furniture and prepared my workspace. Meanwhile, Lucia and others discussed decoration ideas for their rooms, including lighting and color choices. These efforts reflected a coordinated approach to improving both individual and shared spaces.

I then transitioned to the upstairs living room, where I checked my action camera and stand, operated my laptop on the floor, and prepared for equipment calibration. Carrying the corrected calibration board through the living room to the kitchen, I adjusted the action camera’s position, removed and reinserted its SD card, and used my phone to access software and initiate a stopwatch. Using two action cameras, I took multiple photos around the sofa and living room entrance, completing photographic documentation necessary for calibration.

I collected and organized all portable power sources from multiple rooms, systematically unplugging phone chargers, power banks, and charging cables. Starting by unplugging a phone charger and placing items on a table, I proceeded through bedrooms and stairwells to gather all power banks, consolidating them into boxes and onto furniture for efficient management. This ensured that all devices were accounted for and ready for subsequent setup.

Next, I set up camera equipment across the rooms by connecting the collected power banks to charging cables and positioning them near cameras in various locations such as sofas, flower pots, and floors. After each connection, I verified camera status via my phone, moving through areas including the kitchen to monitor device operation. This process ensured all cameras were powered and correctly positioned for recording.

I then managed power banks and cameras by sequentially plugging power banks into camera cables, turning cameras on, and verifying functionality through unplugging and replugging cables as needed. Using my phone, I scanned QR codes to align cameras, standing on stools to hold codes up to cameras while moving through the kitchen. Continuous monitoring of camera statuses confirmed all devices were operational and properly configured.

Controlling camera functions remotely, I scanned QR codes from the sofa and initiated communication by launching WeChat and sending messages via my phone. I connected a laptop with a data cable, checked phone call status, and alternated between keyboard and touchpad operation while multitasking with my phone. Additional cables were plugged into the computer, system status monitored, and equipment functionality confirmed, ensuring integrated device control.

I initiated communication with Lucia by interacting with the laptop, then walked to knock on her bedroom door before sitting on the sofa to discuss. During the conversation, I reviewed camera footage on my phone and coordinated a recording plan involving wearing glasses and simulating a phone call. This aligned team efforts and clarified task execution.

Afterward, I checked power banks by pressing buttons to confirm charge status, placing one on the sofa before lying down to continue laptop work. Later, I shifted to operate a second computer. I answered a phone call instructing the caller to put on glasses, held a power bank, and returned to laptop use. Moving through rooms, I checked equipment and waved at cameras before descending to the first floor, where I observed colleagues preparing food and engaged in brief interactions, including eating a strawberry and speaking with Alice.

Meeting with Alice and Lucia, we discussed completing the task quietly without waking a sleeping individual. We confirmed the person was unresponsive to knocking and agreed to proceed with tidying. I checked power bank charge levels, charged one for Alice, and discussed usage plans with Lucia. Our main objective was to follow the person preparing desserts, accepting limitations without their cooperation. Alice questioned AI understanding, prompting a brief exchange in which I confirmed AI knowledge.

At the stairwell, I informed Alice we could not go upstairs and began descending. After confirming knocking had been done properly, we proceeded downstairs. On the first floor, I entered the kitchen and inquired about tasks. Shure directed me to bring items, marking a transition to active kitchen work.

In the kitchen area, I observed and participated in food preparation. The team discussed ingredient storage and cooking methods such as grilling oysters and baking mangosteen. I picked up and ate fruit during the process while the group coordinated handling ribs, water bottles, and cooking wine. Shure requested assistance filming hand movements. Planning included baking potatoes for dinner and enhancing dishes with cooking wine, supporting meal preparation.

I engaged in light conversation about flavors, secret recipes, and culinary traditions while helping prepare ingredients alongside the team. The dialogue covered cooking excellence and innovation, with recognition of Shure’s progress and originality. This phase emphasized collaborative cooking efforts and thematic reflections.

We planned outdoor grilling, discussing food types and scheduling some tasks for Sunday, including roasting and eating protocols. I confirmed grilling would occur outside where lighting was limited. Together with Alice and Lucia, I assessed outdoor lighting, noting five wall lights and darker areas. We verified that studio lights and fire-starting methods using paper would suffice for the cooking event.

Back inside, I observed ongoing food preparation, including Tasha eating pizza, and received honey from Alice. We discussed washing lettuce, peeling potatoes, opening bottles, and kitchen organization. I inspected a pot and participated in trash sorting as part of cleanup. The team coordinated final preparations and cleaning to support the meal, concluding organized setup and readiness for cooking and filming tasks.

I disposed of trash by placing the garbage bag in the bin, shaking it, and carrying the can outside to leave the bag in a courtyard corner. Returning indoors via the living room to the kitchen, I observed Alice organizing the trash can and Tasha picking up a basin. I proceeded to the poolside faucet to fill and clean a pot. During cleaning, a discussion arose about cooking oysters: Shure insisted on adding oil despite grilling directly without brushing. Frustrated, I discarded oysters and continued cleaning. Unable to find steel wool, I went upstairs to the second-floor kitchen, found and rinsed steel wool near the pool, returned downstairs, and scrubbed the pot thoroughly using steel wool and a steel brush. Lucia raised the need for disposable spoons; Alice offered chopsticks instead. Following Tasha’s guidance, I scrubbed, rinsed, and wiped the pot repeatedly until clean, then handed it to Tasha and moved to the bedroom to check my phone before preparing for the next task.

During a group discussion about utensils and food, I suggested ordering takeout. Alice volunteered to choose items, and we finalized the order collaboratively. Tasha assigned Lucia to retrieve three eggs despite her hesitation. I observed and stood ready to assist. Under Tasha’s instructions, I carefully cracked eggs into a bowl, preserving yolks and avoiding water contamination. I then beat the eggs while Tasha and Lucia monitored, completing egg preparation.

Accompanying Shure and Alice to the courtyard, we attempted to ignite the grill but lacked a flame or suitable ignition source, failing to light charcoal despite trying paper. Shure reignited cardboard inside the kitchen while I shielded flames with a box. We moved burning material outside carefully to avoid fire hazards. The fire burnt out without igniting charcoal. We placed burning cardboard into the oven, added fuel, and tore paper and cardboard to feed flames. I retrieved tongs as directed. Shure questioned the lack of fire accelerant. The fire spread but did not sustain. Meanwhile, I briefly checked my phone and engaged in utensil discussions with Lucia and Alice, holding a bowl and moving toward the bedroom.

Searching for a spoon throughout the guesthouse while holding yogurt, I concluded spoons were unavailable, leading to improvisation. I dismissed the need for chopsticks during a brief talk with Lucia, then observed Tasha cooking and confirmed use of chicken essence. Reviewing the recipe and ingredients with Tasha and Shure, I verbalized steps for milk tea preparation, including adding egg yolks and low-gluten flour. Shure advised higher heat. I examined condensed milk preparation with Tasha, clarifying boiling methods and flavor concentration. After recipe discussion, I inspected food items around the dining area and consulted Katrina on next-day plans involving dancing, pressing flowers, paddling, and shopping for supplies. The group agreed to wait for package arrivals before organizing materials on Saturday, confirming Friday for activities.

I discussed a compression task with Katrina and Lucia, then washed a bowl with Lucia’s help before checking the fire outdoors. Shure inquired about high-concentration alcohol for ignition; Lucia confirmed availability. Noting the furnace probe was insufficiently soaked, I decided to purchase alcohol. Using Meituan on my phone, I ordered alcohol with 30-minute delivery, prioritizing speed despite alternative suggestions. Shure expressed confidence the alcohol would arrive timely.

Returning to the kitchen with my phone, I confirmed arrival time with others and joined Alice, Lucia, and Tasha at the dining table. Receiving the blender, I mixed ingredients at maximum speed under Tasha’s instruction despite splattering. Tasha added sugar, and I coordinated with the group until the mixture was ready. She demonstrated blender handling, noted mixture overfill, and adjusted blending accordingly. I rinsed the stirring rod at the pool faucet while Tasha and Lucia calculated flour amounts to add incrementally. After wiping the rod, I joined discussion covering preparation details, including disallowing oil addition due to remote guidance, flour quantities, and mixture texture concerns.

I engaged Shure about seasoning, learning soy sauce was typically added but had been forgotten due to lack of purchase. Despite my urging, soy sauce was not added. While eating pizza, I conversed with Lucia and Shure about roasting time and recipe similarity, observing Tasha cooking. Checking logistics on my phone, I coordinated supply inquiries with Shure, including alcohol availability. Throughout, I balanced eating, monitoring food preparation, and ensuring communication among participants to maintain task progression.

[DAY3 21:40:00 - DAY3 21:50:00]
I prepared to leave with a cable in hand, initiating a series of interactions with my friends. After pulling out a cable, I indicated my readiness to leave and began walking downstairs, where I encountered Shure. We discussed needing a power strip, and I assured him I would provide a light. Tasha joined, carrying a cable to connect to the socket. Once she plugged it in, I adjusted my position and successfully turned on the light, noting its effectiveness. Meanwhile, Alice commented on the food, and we shared a lighthearted moment about the meal.

As we enjoyed the meal, Shure struggled with opening a wine bottle, which provided entertainment for everyone present. Despite the difficulties, Shure eventually succeeded, and we laughed together. During this time, Katrina and Tasha were also engaged in their activities, and I remained observant while finishing my meal and disposing of the bone.

Moving to a different setting, I joined Tasha and Lucia in a dimly lit room to discuss plans. We began in the kitchen, where I washed my hands and prepared ingredients, including cutting a mango. I coordinated with Tasha, who was also busy preparing ingredients, and we discussed the count of people present. Meanwhile, Lucia assisted with other tasks, and we maintained a steady workflow despite the cluttered kitchen environment.

I continued with food preparation, collaborating with Lucia and Tasha as we managed kitchen tasks. Tasha contributed by placing strawberries on the plate, and Lucia found needed utensils. The atmosphere was lighthearted with jokes and laughter, enhancing the overall experience. We also weighed the prepared fruits, adjusting as necessary to ensure everything was ready.

Throughout this process, I actively engaged with others in the kitchen, coordinating tasks and responding to their needs. With Lucia and Tasha, we maintained a productive and cheerful environment, sharing humorous moments while completing our food preparations. The kitchen was bustling, but we managed to keep everything organized and efficient, with each person contributing to the meal's preparation.

[DAY4 13:09:00 - DAY4 13:12:00]
I searched for and turned on a switch, then checked the display on my phone to monitor the system. I proceeded to another switch, unlocked my phone, and reviewed the screen, pausing and resuming an application as I flipped through items and deleted one. When the software started lagging, I reopened it to maintain functionality, then activated the camera, checked its operation, scrolled through my phone, and clicked the camera again to ensure proper setup.

I instructed Nicous to unplug the power bank and all related devices. Nicous moved a stool, sat down, and put on his shoes while I continued scrolling and tapping through my phone. I questioned the situation, then picked up the power bank and pulled it out. I explained to Nicous that the device was related to a new currency called "gold coins," which had been hidden for a long time and was being used for the first time now.

I plugged the power bank into another device and placed it on the ground. Then, I adjusted the camera by pulling it down and plugging it in as well. While Nicous retrieved something nearby, I walked to the table and took down another item. Shure commented on it being a "first-class historical issue" and a social problem. I unplugged the device and set it on the ground, informing Nicous that after unplugging, there was no need to plug in a new one immediately, just to leave it charging and plug in the new device in the afternoon.

I moved around the room searching for more devices, taking them down, then walked toward the kitchen but found nothing else. Gathering electric wires in my hands, I walked away and handed one to Nicous, instructing him to go upstairs. I asked him to help deliver the wire to "that Lure." Meanwhile, I plugged the wires into the power line, searched for spare lines, and inserted another one to complete the setup.
